evidence_packet.evidence_text: Doorman who witnessed racist outburst says abuse 'becoming normal' - BBC News Image caption, Jawad Ali, 20, said he now expects racial abuse when he goes to work By Kaya Black North West Published 1 hour ago A doorman who shared a video of a racist outburst he witnessed while at work has said such abuse towards staff is becoming "normalised". The footage, taken outside Ko-Ko Lounge in Rochdale, Greater Manchester, showed a woman shouting abuse and making gestures at a black security guard. Jawad Ali said the club-goer became abusive after being asked to move away from an exit while he was working at the venue on Saturday night. Greater Manchester Police said it had received a report about the incident and inquiries were ongoing. Image caption, Footage of the incident has been shared widely online "It's disgusting," said Jawad, 20, who was working for Protective One Security at the time. He alleged the woman had also directed racial abuse towards him before the filming. Jawad said he decided to post the video on social media because "you can't do that and get away with it". "This isn't the first time, and it won't be the last," he added. Jawad said during the past two years working on the doors he has been called every racial slur and even threatened with death. "I expect now when I come to work to be racially abused one night out of the four that I work," he continued. "Its a normal thing now. It should be a big thing that gets prosecuted heavily." Image caption, The incident happened outside Ko-Ko Lounge in Rochdale Fellow security worker Liz Turley, who works for Radius Security, said: "There hasn't been a night where I haven't experienced some instance of somebody standing there for a prolonged period of time giving me abuse." evidence_packet.evidence_text: Social media a factor in HMO attacks, says police boss - BBC News Image source, LDRS/MEN Image caption, Police said there had been 46 properties damaged across the city region since 5 October By Naj Modak , North West and Ed Barnes , Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 1 hour ago Social media is in part behind a spate of recent "racially or religiously motivated" attacks on houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) across Greater Manchester, a senior police officer has said. Greater Manchester Police said there had been 46 properties damaged across the city region since 5 October, including in Salford, Tameside and Stockport. Ch Sup Marcus Noden said footage of criminal damage was being shared widely "followed by comments and discussions", and people were using social media to "push the message out across different areas". He warned people to stop the attacks, which he said were "unlawful, reckless and putting lives at risk". As an investigation into the run of criminal damage continues, a 33-year-old man was arrested on Wednesday morning on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage and remained in custody for questioning. The damage was to HMOs or properties that were mistaken for HMOs. In Salford, 41 properties were targeted with three in Tameside and two in Stockport over the period. Image source, LDRS/MEN Image caption, Windows are seen boarded up on one property due to concerns of further attacks According to the Local Democracy Reporting Service , last week, two properties in Heaton Norris just outside Stockport town centre were targeted with anti-HMO graffiti. title: Women targeted by police officers who 'abused the badge'

evidence_packet.title: Women targeted by police officers who 'abused the badge'
evidence_packet.lead: Two women preyed upon by serving police officers describe their ordeals and why they are speaking out
evidence_packet.summary: Two women preyed upon by serving police officers describe their ordeals and why they are speaking out
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Two women who were preyed upon by serving police officers they trusted have described their ordeals and why they decided to speak out Naomi Meadows was raped by a detective she met online in Devon, while Catherine Dobson was subjected to years of coercive and controlling behaviour by a Lancashire police officer who worked in a sexual offences unit Catherine said: "He used his job, he used his power and he abused the badge. Whatever his motives were, I will never understand." The women waived their right to anonymity to tell their harrowing stories as part of a BBC investigation that uncovered more than 1,200 domestic abuse allegations made in three years against police officers and special constables across England and Wales Professional standards investigations were opened into allegations including rape, sexual assault, grievous bodily harm, stalking and serious violence Most cases were discontinued, subjected to no further action or dropped because of a lack of evidence or victims withdrawing their complaints

title: Inquest hears of 'great danger' tip-off before fire murders

evidence_packet.title: Inquest hears of 'great danger' tip-off before fire murders
evidence_packet.lead: Social workers were told children were in "great danger" days before a fatal fire, an inquest hears
evidence_packet.summary: Social workers were told children were in "great danger" days before a fatal fire, an inquest hears
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Social workers received an anonymous tip-off that children were in "great danger" days before they were murdered in an arson attack, an inquest heard Demi Pearson, 14, her brother, Brandon, eight, and sisters, Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, died after petrol bombs were thrown into their home on Jackson Street, Walkden, Salford, in the early hours of December 11, 2017 Their mother Michelle Pearson, 37, died almost two years later after suffering severe burns A joint inquest into their deaths, now in its third week, is being heard at Bolton Coroners' Court and on Wednesday it heard of social services involvement with the family The hearing was told on 29 November, 2017, less than two weeks before the fatal attack, the social services department at Salford City Council received an anonymous call The caller said: "The children are in a really unsafe environment and in great danger."

title: Sinkhole revealed 50 metre deep mine shaft uneder road

evidence_packet.title: Sinkhole revealed 50 metre deep mine shaft uneder road
evidence_packet.lead: Part of Alan Turing Way has been closed since March and is expected to stay shut until mid-December
evidence_packet.summary: Part of Alan Turing Way has been closed since March and is expected to stay shut until mid-December
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Sinkhole revealed 50 metre deep mine shaft uneder road - BBC News Image caption, A sinkhole found in March revealed a 50m deep sinkhole By Kevin Fitzpatrick and Rebecca Brahde , North West Published 21 October 2026 Work is taking place to repair a sinkhole which revealed a 50m (164ft) mine shaft under a busy road in east Manchester. Part of the northbound carriageway on Alan Turing Way has been closed since March, when the road surface began to sink. Since then, Manchester City Council has filled the hole with more than 100 tonnes of concrete. It said it expected the route to be open again December. Image caption, Councillor Mandie Shilton Godwin says it has been a "massive job" Mandie Shilton Godwin, the executive member for transport, said it had been a "massive job", adding it had "taken an awfully long time”. She added: "It started in March when the depression was noticed, but it wasn't until the end of September when the team were absolutely sure what the problem was. "Once they were sure what the problem was, then they could begin to put it right. "No one could have anticipated the scale of the void that we found but, once it became apparent, all of our effort went into making sure the site was safe and the road could be reopened." A concrete cap is currently being put over the mine shaft. Work will then need to take place to fill the remaining void beneath the road, and lay a new surface. evidence_packet.title: Three more arrests in Alisha Samuels murder investigation
evidence_packet.lead: Alisha Samuels, 26, was found dead after a disturbance in the Newton Heath area of Manchester
evidence_packet.summary: Alisha Samuels, 26, was found dead after a disturbance in the Newton Heath area of Manchester
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Three more arrests in Alisha Samuels murder investigation - BBC News Image source, Family photo Image caption, Alisha Samuels was found dead following a disturbance in the Newton Heath area By Rebecca Brahde North West Published 21 October 2026 Three more arrests have been made in connection with the suspected murder of a woman who was stabbed in a street in Manchester. Alisha Samuels, 26, was found dead after officers were called to a disturbance on Dorking Avenue in the Newton Heath area of the city at about 02:00 BST on Thursday. On Tuesday, Lawrence Johnson, 26, of Dorking Avenue, was charged with the murder of Samuels and the attempted murder of a man. Earlier two men, both 19, were arrested on suspicion of murder and a 48-year-old woman was held on suspicion of assisting an offender, Greater Manchester Police said. Det Ch Insp Justin Bryant said: "We remain focused on establishing the full circumstances and want to reassure Alisha's loved ones that we are committed to securing justice for her. "My thoughts remain with Alisha's family and friends as they continue to come to terms with this devastating loss." The detective renewed an appeal for witnesses or anyone with information to come forward. evidence_packet.evidence_text: North West health correspondent Published 21 October 2026 Younger adults living in the North of England are 42% more likely to die than their counterparts in the South, according to new research A study by academics in Manchester and Liverpool found people in the North aged 25 to 49 faced a significantly higher risk of death than people of the same age living in the South Researchers said deprivation was a major factor behind the gap and called for urgent action to tackle inequalities The Department of Health and Social Care (DoHSC) said it was determined to reduce health inequalities and close the divide The research, by the University of Manchester, the University of Liverpool and Health Equity North and published in The Lancet medical journal , external , analysed deaths between 1981 and 2024 in two geographical areas of England, splitting England's population into "two roughly The North encompassed Greater Manchester, Cheshire, Lancashire, Yorkshire, Cumbria, the North East and the East and West Midlands, while the South covered London and the South East, the East and the South West

title: Wigan council 'listening' as warehouse plans dropped

evidence_packet.title: Wigan council 'listening' as warehouse plans dropped
evidence_packet.lead: Wigan Council said it had listened and "struck the right balance" between supporting growth and creating jobs
evidence_packet.summary: Wigan Council said it had listened and "struck the right balance" between supporting growth and creating jobs
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan council 'listening' as warehouse plans dropped - BBC News Image source, Joanna Allsop Image caption, Members of the Save Our Astley and Boothstown Greenbelt at a summer protest By Kevin Fitzpatrick North West Published 21 October 2026 A consultation is due to end on Wigan Council's plan for future development, with four sites potentially earmarked for warehouses being removed. It follows an outcry from residents over the construction of huge warehouses close to homes near Astley. The local authority said it had listened and "struck the right balance between supporting economic growth and job creation". Greenbelt campaigners and opposition councillors claimed they had forced the council to act. Councils must put together a local plan which identifies sites for housing and business development every decade or so and Wigan is in the process of updating its own. In the version under consultation, it has said four sites would not be taken forward. They include to the north of M6 junction 26, Moss Industrial Estate extension, Bridgewater West in Astley, and West of Winwick Lane in Lowton. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Two women who were preyed upon by serving police officers they trusted have described their ordeals and why they decided to speak out Naomi Meadows was raped by a detective she met online in Devon, while Catherine Dobson was subjected to years of coercive and controlling behaviour by a Lancashire police officer who worked in a sexual offences unit Catherine said: "He used his job, he used his power and he abused the badge. Whatever his motives were, I will never understand." The women waived their right to anonymity to tell their harrowing stories as part of a BBC investigation that uncovered more than 1,200 domestic abuse allegations made in three years against police officers and special constables across England and Wales Professional standards investigations were opened into allegations including rape, sexual assault, grievous bodily harm, stalking and serious violence Most cases were discontinued, subjected to no further action or dropped because of a lack of evidence or victims withdrawing their complaints

evidence_packet.lead: Social workers received an anonymous tip-off that children were in "great danger" days before they were murdered in an arson attack, an inquest heard Demi Pearson, 14, her brother, Brandon, eight, and sisters, Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, died after petrol bombs were thrown into

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Social workers received an anonymous tip-off that children were in "great danger" days before they were murdered in an arson attack, an inquest heard Demi Pearson, 14, her brother, Brandon, eight, and sisters, Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, died after petrol bombs were thrown into their home on Jackson Street, Walkden, Salford, in the early hours of December 11, 2017 Their mother Michelle Pearson, 37, died almost two years later after suffering severe burns A joint inquest into their deaths, now in its third week, is being heard at Bolton Coroners' Court and on Wednesday it heard of social services involvement with the family The hearing was told on 29 November, 2017, less than two weeks before the fatal attack, the social services department at Salford City Council received an anonymous call The caller said: "The children are in a really unsafe environment and in great danger."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The leader of Manchester City Council has said there will be no extra cash for restoring the city's historic Town Hall The project's original budget was £330m but has since risen to almost £525m, following delays and unexpected problems during the restoration Garry Bridges said the project was now coming in on its revised budget and there would be "no more increases" The Grade I-listed Victorian building closed in 2018 for the work, which was initially expected to be completed by 2024. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester National Poppy Appeal launches at Manchester Victoria station with new 'Spitfire poppies' Metal from an RAF Spitfire has been used to craft four special poppies Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 06:31, 22 Oct 2026 The annual national Poppy Appeal was being launched in Manchester today ahead of Remembrance Sunday next month. And this year's launch will involve four specially created poppies - each one crafted from the metal of iconic Second World War RAF Spitfire fighter planes The launch of the Royal British Legion's appeal marks the start of the national period of remembrance, when the nation wears the red poppy to remember the service and sacrifice of armed forces personnel. All funds raised will be used by the legion to support veterans and their fa The poppy became a symbol of remembrance and hope for a peaceful future in the aftermath of the First World War. Since 1921, the legion's army of volunteer collectors has been at the heart of the annual appeal Remembrance Sunday will this year be observed on Sunday, November 8 with Armistice Day, which marks the end of the First World War, falling on Wednesday, November 11 The Royal British Legion said this year's appeal would 'shine a light on Armed Forces families, recognising the unique challenges and sacrifices they make in support of their loved ones who serve'. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Inside the glamourous Art Deco Salford home given listed status Broughton Park property is 91 years old Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 06:18, 22 Oct 2026 Updated 06:36, 22 Oct 2026 View 5 Images The 1935 hou A family home in Salford has been given Grade II listed status. The property on Old Hall Lane, Broughton Park, is described by experts as a "strikingly glamourous" house Built in 1935 it is a rare example of the international Streamline Moderne style that evolved from Art Deco. It features curved corners, long horizontal "speed lines," and a sleek, machine-age look inspired by ocean liners, airplanes, and trains Other examples of the style include East Finchley Tube Station in London and the Coca Cola building in Los Angeles. The design is characterised by flat roofs, horizontal emphasis, curved corners and dramatic glazing From the outside, this house is distinguished by slim brown brick facades, a flat roof, an exposed white concrete base, and windows that span both curved and angled corners View 5 Images A curved stair tower dominates the back of the house, while the entrance front steps back in stages, with an original single-storey garage reflecting the growing importance of the car in home design between the First and Second World Wars

Many were left confined to their cabins during the eight-night trip, while others were hospitalised when they returned back to the UK The group have now instructed international injury lawyers to investigate their illnesses. P&O said they are 'aware' of groups correspondence and 'take such reports seriously' Julie Stones, 53, from Bolton, was among those who fell ill. She said the illness left her battling a catalogue of health problems

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester National Poppy Appeal launches at Manchester Victoria station with new 'Spitfire poppies' Metal from an RAF Spitfire has been used to craft four special poppies Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 06:31, 22 Oct 2026 The annual national Poppy Appeal was being launched in Manchester today ahead of Remembrance Sunday next month. And this year's launch will involve four specially created poppies - each one crafted from the metal of iconic Second World War RAF Spitfire fighter planes The launch of the Royal British Legion's appeal marks the start of the national period of remembrance, when the nation wears the red poppy to remember the service and sacrifice of armed forces personnel. All funds raised will be used by the legion to support veterans and their fa The poppy became a symbol of remembrance and hope for a peaceful future in the aftermath of the First World War. Since 1921, the legion's army of volunteer collectors has been at the heart of the annual appeal Remembrance Sunday will this year be observed on Sunday, November 8 with Armistice Day, which marks the end of the First World War, falling on Wednesday, November 11 The Royal British Legion said this year's appeal would 'shine a light on Armed Forces families, recognising the unique challenges and sacrifices they make in support of their loved ones who serve'. The 2026 appeal aims to raise £50m

evidence_packet.title: Inside the glamourous Art Deco Salford home given listed status
evidence_packet.lead: Salford Inside the glamourous Art Deco Salford home given listed status Broughton Park property is 91 years old Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 06:18, 22 Oct 2026 Updated 06:36, 22 Oct 2026 View 5 Images The 1935 hou A family home in Salford has
evidence_packet.summary: Salford Inside the glamourous Art Deco Salford home given listed status Broughton Park property is 91 years old Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 06:18, 22 Oct 2026 Updated 06:36, 22 Oct 2026 View 5 Images The 1935 hou A family home in Salford has
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Inside the glamourous Art Deco Salford home given listed status Broughton Park property is 91 years old Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 06:18, 22 Oct 2026 Updated 06:36, 22 Oct 2026 View 5 Images The 1935 hou A family home in Salford has been given Grade II listed status. The property on Old Hall Lane, Broughton Park, is described by experts as a "strikingly glamourous" house Built in 1935 it is a rare example of the international Streamline Moderne style that evolved from Art Deco. It features curved corners, long horizontal "speed lines," and a sleek, machine-age look inspired by ocean liners, airplanes, and trains Other examples of the style include East Finchley Tube Station in London and the Coca Cola building in Los Angeles. The design is characterised by flat roofs, horizontal emphasis, curved corners and dramatic glazing From the outside, this house is distinguished by slim brown brick facades, a flat roof, an exposed white concrete base, and windows that span both curved and angled corners View 5 Images A curved stair tower dominates the back of the house, while the entrance front steps back in stages, with an original single-storey garage reflecting the growing importance of the car in home design between the First and Second World Wars

evidence_packet.summary: Courts Man who stabbed pregnant girlfriend to death after she told him she had aborted their twins tells murder trial he 'snapped' Stephan Garner denies murdering Amber O’Brien Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 06:05, 22 Oct A man who stabbed his pregna
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Man who stabbed pregnant girlfriend to death after she told him she had aborted their twins tells murder trial he 'snapped' Stephan Garner denies murdering Amber O’Brien Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 06:05, 22 Oct A man who stabbed his pregnant girlfriend to death claimed he ‘snapped’ after she told him she’d had an abortion, a murder trial has heard Stephan Garner, 31, has admitted killing 33-year-old Amber O’Brien - who was expecting twins - but denies murdering her. Garner killed Ms O’Brien in his flat in Blackley, north Manchester, after the pair had argued, jurors at Manchester Crown Court have heard Ms O’Brien’s body was left on the bathroom floor of an eighth floor flat in Blackley, where she had been living with Garner, the father to her nine-week-old unborn twins. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Murder accused said 'he's under the car' after hitting Stretford Grammar headteacher, trial told by cousin who was in Volvo Simon Richardson, 35, denies murdering Michael Mullins as he cycled home from work Add to preferred sources News Amy Wal The cousin of the man accused of murdering Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins told jurors the defendant knew the tragic cyclist was under his car as he was dragged to his death while she watched from the passenger seat Gabrielle Debotte, who was in Simon Richardson's Volvo, said he told her 'he's under the car' before she heard 'moaning' from beneath the car. Mr Richardson, 35, is accused of hitting popular educator Michael Mullins as he cycled home from work on April 20 Prosecutors allege Mr Richardson did not stop and 'put his foot down', dragging 56-year-old Mr Mullins along the road for 2.2km - 1.3 miles - before leaving him to die on a grass verge on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm Jurors previously heard witnesses described seeing Mr Richardson's Volvo ‘absolutely tanking it’ towards the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane Mr Richardson denies murder; an alternate offence of manslaughter; and dangerous driving. He is on trial at Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court

evidence_packet.summary: Manchester The mammoth job of fixing the giant hole on Alan Turing Way after mineshaft uncovered The section of road through Alan Turing Way has been closed off since March, when a giant hole appeared out of nowhere Add to preferred sources Comments N The northbound section of th
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester The mammoth job of fixing the giant hole on Alan Turing Way after mineshaft uncovered The section of road through Alan Turing Way has been closed off since March, when a giant hole appeared out of nowhere Add to preferred sources Comments N The northbound section of the road between Ashton Old Road and Grey Mare Lane has been shut off ever since. For months the council wasn’t entirely sure what had caused the stretch of road to collapse But in September, engineers discovered it was a 50m deep mine shaft under the road that triggered the 3m wide crater There is a long history of mining and colliers throughout east Manchester, but this mineshaft wasn’t recorded on historic maps and took workers completely by surprise Further investigations revealed the extent of the cavity and scale of repairs required, which is a process that has taken since March to complete View 4 Images Work going on at the giant hole on Alan Turing Way in East Manchester (Image: LDRS)

evidence_packet.lead: Bury Street lights, council tax, school crossing patrols and bins - the 'distasteful' decisions as Bury council scrambles to plug £20m black hole New details have been revealed and the council wants to know what you think View Image A number of cost-c Add to preferred sources Com
evidence_packet.summary: Bury Street lights, council tax, school crossing patrols and bins - the 'distasteful' decisions as Bury council scrambles to plug £20m black hole New details have been revealed and the council wants to know what you think View Image A number of cost-c Add to preferred sources Com
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury Street lights, council tax, school crossing patrols and bins - the 'distasteful' decisions as Bury council scrambles to plug £20m black hole New details have been revealed and the council wants to know what you think View Image A number of cost-c Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 16:37, 21 Oct 2026 New details have been released on Bury council’s savings plans after town hall bosses warned ‘distasteful’ decisions have to be made The local authority is facing a difficult financial situation, with a £20m budget gap identified for the coming financial year if no action is taken. Bosses believe they have identified a way to reduce that gap to around £9.6m through a number of cost cutting and revenue raising The measures have previously been described as ‘regrettable’ and ‘distasteful’ by finance lead Sean Thorpe. However, ‘all options’ have to be considered, he said These include measures around garden waste, street lighting, social care payments, school crossing patrols and leisure charges. The authority had also been considering cuts to youth services, but has now said it will not be doing this after finding an alternative way to fund them The authority’s executive last week signed off on entering into conversations with the Government over Exceptional Financial Support (EFS) to help bridge the remaining gap. EFS allows town halls greater flexibility when it comes to meeting expenses

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Travel 'Our £3k Mediterranean cruise was meant to be a celebration, it turned into a nightmare' A number of women from Greater Manchester, who paid up to £3,000 each, fell seriously ill onboard the P&O ship Add to preferred sources News Ed Chatterton A group of passengers from Greater Manchester who booked a P&O cruise to celebrate a 60th birthday say their trip turned into a 'nightmare' after they fell seriously ill onboard The group, some from Bolton, Bury and Wigan, were struck down with gastric illness and flu-like symptoms while travelling around the Greek islands on the P&O Azura between May 28 and June 4 this year. The holidaymakers, who paid up to £3,000 each, claim they encountered an 'overp They said they raised concerns about hygiene in buffet restaurants where flies could be seen around uncovered food. Many were left confined to their cabins during the eight-night trip, while others were hospitalised when they returned back to the UK The group have now instructed international injury lawyers to investigate their illnesses. P&O said they are 'aware' of groups correspondence and 'take such reports seriously' Julie Stones, 53, from Bolton, was among those who fell ill. She said the illness left her battling a catalogue of health problems

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Inside the glamourous Art Deco Salford home given listed status Broughton Park property is 91 years old Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 06:18, 22 Oct 2026 Updated 06:36, 22 Oct 2026 View 5 Images The 1935 hou A family home in Salford has been given Grade II listed status. The property on Old Hall Lane, Broughton Park, is described by experts as a "strikingly glamourous" house Built in 1935 it is a rare example of the international Streamline Moderne style that evolved from Art Deco. It features curved corners, long horizontal "speed lines," and a sleek, machine-age look inspired by ocean liners, airplanes, and trains Other examples of the style include East Finchley Tube Station in London and the Coca Cola building in Los Angeles. The design is characterised by flat roofs, horizontal emphasis, curved corners and dramatic glazing From the outside, this house is distinguished by slim brown brick facades, a flat roof, an exposed white concrete base, and windows that span both curved and angled corners View 5 Images A curved stair tower dominates the back of the house, while the entrance front steps back in stages, with an original single-storey garage reflecting the growing importance of the car in home design between the First and Second World Wars

evidence_texts: Salford Inside the glamourous Art Deco Salford home given listed status Broughton Park property is 91 years old Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 06:18, 22 Oct 2026 Updated 06:36, 22 Oct 2026 View 5 Images The 1935 hou A family home in Salford has been given Grade II listed status. The property on Old Hall Lane, Broughton Park, is described by experts as a "strikingly glamourous" house Built in 1935 it is a rare example of the international Streamline Moderne style that evolved from Art Deco. It features curved corners, long horizontal "speed lines," and a sleek, machine-age look inspired by ocean liners, airplanes, and trains Other examples of the style include East Finchley Tube Station in London and the Coca Cola building in Los Angeles. The design is characterised by flat roofs, horizontal emphasis, curved corners and dramatic glazing From the outside

evidence_packet.title: National Poppy Appeal launches at Manchester Victoria station with new 'Spitfire poppies'
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester National Poppy Appeal launches at Manchester Victoria station with new 'Spitfire poppies' Metal from an RAF Spitfire has been used to craft four special poppies Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 06:31, 22 Oct 2026 The annual national Poppy Ap
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester National Poppy Appeal launches at Manchester Victoria station with new 'Spitfire poppies' Metal from an RAF Spitfire has been used to craft four special poppies Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 06:31, 22 Oct 2026 The annual national Poppy Ap
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester National Poppy Appeal launches at Manchester Victoria station with new 'Spitfire poppies' Metal from an RAF Spitfire has been used to craft four special poppies Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 06:31, 22 Oct 2026 The annual national Poppy Appeal was being launched in Manchester today ahead of Remembrance Sunday next month. And this year's launch will involve four specially created poppies - each one crafted from the metal of iconic Second World War RAF Spitfire fighter planes The launch of the Royal British Legion's appeal marks the start of the national period of remembrance, when the nation wears the red poppy to remember the service and sacrifice of armed forces personnel. All funds raised will be used by the legion to support veterans and their fa The poppy became a symbol of remembrance and hope for a peaceful future in the aftermath of the First World War. Since 1921, the legion's army of volunteer collectors has been at the heart of the annual appeal Remembrance Sunday will this year be observed on Sunday, November 8 with Armistice Day, which marks the end of the First World War, falling on Wednesday, November 11 The Royal British Legion said this year's appeal would 'shine a light on Armed Forces families, recognising the unique challenges and sacrifices they make in support of their loved ones who serve'. The 2026 appeal aims to raise £50m

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan A heritage tearoom wants to open until 10pm for 12 nights a year but the neighbours aren't happy Merly’s Kitchen, which operates within a Grade II-listed building in Astley has faced opposition to its plans Add to preferred sources Comments News A application for a ‘heritage tea room’ to open until 10pm a dozen nights a year has seen multiple objections from neighbours. Merly’s Kitchen, occupies part of the ground floor of Damhouse, a Grade II-listed building at Astley Hall Drive, Astley Morts Astley Heritage Trust, a charity that operates the Damhouse, currently has a licence for Merly’s to operate from 8am to 8pm Next week Wigan council’s planning committee will deliberate on an application to vary those opening hours to 10pm for up to 12 evenings per year The Damhouse is presently home to 14 businesses including a nursery The site has significant historical importance, having originally served as a manor house before later being used as a hospital

She was naked, ‘cold to the touch’, and was covered in a blue tarpaulin lying in ‘pools of water’ A pathologist later found she had suffered more than 60 separate stab, incised and puncture wounds, 32, of which were to her face and neck, during the attack in the early hours of April 18. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Murder accused said 'he's under the car' after hitting Stretford Grammar headteacher, trial told by cousin who was in Volvo Simon Richardson, 35, denies murdering Michael Mullins as he cycled home from work Add to preferred sources News Amy Wal The cousin of the man accused of murdering Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins told jurors the defendant knew the tragic cyclist was under his car as he was dragged to his death while she watched from the passenger seat Gabrielle Debotte, who was in Simon Richardson's Volvo, said he told her 'he's under the car' before she heard 'moaning' from beneath the car. Mr Richardson, 35, is accused of hitting popular educator Michael Mullins as he cycled home from work on April 20 Prosecutors allege Mr Richardson did not stop and 'put his foot down', dragging 56-year-old Mr Mullins along the road for 2.2km - 1.3 miles - before leaving him to die on a grass verge on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm Jurors previously heard witnesses described seeing Mr Richardson's Volvo ‘absolutely tanking it’ towards the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane Mr Richardson denies murder; an alternate offence of manslaughter; and dangerous driving. He is on trial at Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester The mammoth job of fixing the giant hole on Alan Turing Way after mineshaft uncovered The section of road through Alan Turing Way has been closed off since March, when a giant hole appeared out of nowhere Add to preferred sources Comments N The northbound section of the road between Ashton Old Road and Grey Mare Lane has been shut off ever since. For months the council wasn’t entirely sure what had caused the stretch of road to collapse But in September, engineers discovered it was a 50m deep mine shaft under the road that triggered the 3m wide crater There is a long history of mining and colliers throughout east Manchester, but this mineshaft wasn’t recorded on historic maps and took workers completely by surprise Further investigations revealed the extent of the cavity and scale of repairs required, which is a process that has taken since March to complete View 4 Images Work going on at the giant hole on Alan Turing Way in East Manchester (Image: LDRS)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury Street lights, council tax, school crossing patrols and bins - the 'distasteful' decisions as Bury council scrambles to plug £20m black hole New details have been revealed and the council wants to know what you think View Image A number of cost-c Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 16:37, 21 Oct 2026 New details have been released on Bury council’s savings plans after town hall bosses warned ‘distasteful’ decisions have to be made The local authority is facing a difficult financial situation, with a £20m budget gap identified for the coming financial year if no action is taken. Bosses believe they have identified a way to reduce that gap to around £9.6m through a number of cost cutting and revenue raising The measures have previously been described as ‘regrettable’ and ‘distasteful’ by finance lead Sean Thorpe. However, ‘all options’ have to be considered, he said These include measures around garden waste, street lighting, social care payments, school crossing patrols and leisure charges. The authority had also been considering cuts to youth services, but has now said it will not be doing this after finding an alternative way to fund them The authority’s executive last week signed off on entering into conversations with the Government over Exceptional Financial Support (EFS) to help bridge the remaining gap. EFS allows town halls greater flexibility when it comes to meeting expenses

A 26-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of murder In an update issued this morning (October 21), GMP said she had since been detained under Section 2 of the Mental Health Act. Yvonne's family issued a moving tribute to her on Tuesday evening, while releasing a photo of her alongside her beloved partner, Tom Grant They said: "Yvonne was a much-loved mum, Nana, sister and auntie, known for her caring heart, strength and kindness. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wednesday 21 October 2026 at 6:20pm Four children died after petrol bombs were thrown into their home in Salford in 2017, their mother died two years later after suffering severe burns. Social workers received an anonymous tip-off that children were in “great danger” days before Demi Pearson, 14, her brother, Brandon, eight, and sisters, Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, died after petrol bombs were thrown into their home on Jackson Street, Walkden, Salford, in the early hours of December 11, 2017 Their mother Michelle Pearson, 37, died almost two years later after suffering severe burns A joint inquest into their deaths, now in its third week, is ongoing at Bolton Coroners’ Court and on Wednesday it heard of social services involvement with the family The hearing was told that on November 29, 2017, less than two weeks before the fatal attack, the social services department at Salford City Council received an anonymous call The caller said: “The children are in a really unsafe environment and in great danger.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: In Manchester, football betting once meant checking the odds in a shop window, filling out a paper slip and returning later to collect any winnings. Betting shops remain part of the city, but smartphones have made those visits optional. Live odds, match statistics and promotional Traditional betting shops offer a particular experience: printed racing information, televised sport and face-to-face conversations. A customer can ask about a market and leave with a physical receipt. That social element is difficult to reproduce on a phone, especially around bu Yet the nationwide shop network has contracted. Figures for the financial year ending March 2026 show 5,617 betting shops in Great Britain, down 3.6% from a year earlier. The number describes the national market, not a count of closures in Manchester. Those totals also conceal re The most obvious difference is timing. In a shop, a bet is often arranged before kickoff or during a visit. On a phone, customers can check a market while following the match from a sofa, pub or stadium concourse. In-play odds may change after a goal, red card or substitution, so Mobile access also changes which information bettors see. A fixture page can display team form, corners, shots and several markets without requiring a conversation at the counter. But quick access should not be confused with better predictions: a statistic helps describe a match, The industry’s financial figures show why mobile deserves attention. Remote betting generated £2.4 billion in gross gambling yield during 2025–26, while betting conducted outside remote channels also generated about £2.4 billion. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Naomi Meadows was raped by a detective she met online in Devon, while Catherine Dobson was subjected to years of coercive and controlling behaviour by a Lancashire police officer who worked in a sexual offences unit Catherine said: "He used his job, he used his power and he abused the badge. Whatever his motives were, I will never understand." The women waived their right to anonymity to tell their harrowing stories as part of a BBC investigation that uncovered more than 1,200 domestic abuse allegations made in three years against police officers and special constables across England and Wales Professional standards investigations were opened into allegations including rape, sexual assault, grievous bodily harm, stalking and serious violence Most cases were discontinued, subjected to no further action or dropped because of a lack of evidence or victims withdrawing their complaints Campaigners say more needs to be done to tackle police-perpetrated abuse despite repeated warnings about failures to identify and remove dangerous officers in the wake of the 2021 murder of Sarah Everard in London by serving Metropolitan Police officer Wayne Couzens

evidence_packet.summary: Demi Pearson, 14, her brother, Brandon, eight, and sisters, Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, died after petrol bombs were thrown into their home on Jackson Street, Walkden, Salford, in the early hours of December 11, 2017 Their mother Michelle Pearson, 37, died almost two years late
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Demi Pearson, 14, her brother, Brandon, eight, and sisters, Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, died after petrol bombs were thrown into their home on Jackson Street, Walkden, Salford, in the early hours of December 11, 2017 Their mother Michelle Pearson, 37, died almost two years later after suffering severe burns A joint inquest into their deaths, now in its third week, is being heard at Bolton Coroners' Court and on Wednesday it heard of social services involvement with the family The hearing was told on 29 November, 2017, less than two weeks before the fatal attack, the social services department at Salford City Council received an anonymous call The caller said: "The children are in a really unsafe environment and in great danger." Georgina Tighe, a social work manager at the local authority, said the call was taken by an administrative person working in the department and the information was never passed on to her as it should have been

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A passenger in a car that dragged a head teacher to his death for more than a mile has told a murder trial the driver could hear the victim from inside the vehicle after hitting him Gabrielle Debotte said she "still had visions" of the moment her cousin, Simon Richardson, hit 56-year-old cyclist Michael Mullins at 18:07 BST on 20 April before driving away Giving evidence from behind a screen, Ms Debotte told Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court that Richardson spent the night after the crash "laughing and joking" and drinking alcohol Richardson, 35, denies murder and an alternative count of manslaughter The jury heard Mr Mullins was trapped under the vehicle and dragged 2.2km (1.3 miles) The married father-of-two was found injured by a motorcyclist who had followed a trail of blood from near the crash site on Paddock Lane to Wet Gate Lane. Mr Mullins died a short time later

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Council is introducing new orders to tackle anti-social behaviour in Wigan and Leigh town centres, including targeted powers against e-bikes and scooters These Public Space Protection Orders (PSPOs) will be in place for three years to support the police, council and other authorities in tackling a wide range of issues, reduce crime and help people feel safer in their communities This introduction follows an extensive review of previous orders and a public consultation held over the summer which gathered significant feedback from residents, businesses and the community sector Councillor Kevin Anderson, cabinet portfolio holder for Police, Crime and Civil Contingencies, said: “Residents, businesses and visitors all took part in our consultation, and it was clear that anti-social behaviour remains a concern “Most people who visit, live and work in our town centres do so responsibly, and these orders are aimed at addressing the small number of behaviours that negatively impact our communities, while ensuring support remains available for those who may be vulnerable.” The orders prohibit several anti-social behaviours, with new powers to enforce against anti-social use of cycles, e-bikes and scooters, and drug-related litter and paraphernalia

evidence_packet.evidence_text: We know residents have questions about the future of Gibfield and recent activity around the site. This update explains the current position, what survey activity means and how local people can take part in any future planning process In August 2026, Wigan Council’s Cabinet agreed to object to Peel Land’s proposed Gibfield Park masterplan. Cabinet’s position was that the housing and industrial proposals were not acceptable in their current form and did not have cabinet members’ support. No planning application West of Gibfield was allocated for homes, employment and green space through Places for Everyone, which was adopted in 2024 and now forms part of the statutory development plan. The current Wigan Local Plan process cannot reverse that allocation. However, allocation does not gran Our chief executive has written to the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, requesting Gibfield to be removed from the plan. We are waiting for a response Cabinet has formally objected to the proposed masterplan and made clear that it cannot support the development now or in the future Peel Land may undertake ecology surveys, ground-condition testing, environmental work and traffic or transport studies to understand the site and prepare evidence. These investigations do not mean planning permission has been granted or that a future application will be approved

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

title: Beat the Jams Autumn season announced

evidence_packet.title: Beat the Jams Autumn season announced
evidence_packet.lead: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians.
evidence_packet.summary: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live […] The post Beat the Jams Autumn season announced appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. Please email learning@bandonthewall.org if you have any questions about this course

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Olllam is a band that fuses Irish traditional music with the modern jazz/post-rock energy of Detroit. evidence_packet.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital

evidence_packet.title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital
evidence_packet.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
evidence_packet.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Ecommerce Leeds Shopify Premier Partner undertakes epic ecommerce replatform for multi-brand home AV retailer Tech JustGiving launch advisor and erstwile Greenpeace fundraising director among latest appointments at Manchester charitytech Agency Ex-WPP AI trio launch out-of-box pr One-in-ten (11%) UK adults have now used TotallyMoney, which helps people improve their credit status, qualify for lower-cost credit and unlock a broader range of financial products TotallyMoney provides people with access to their live credit score and credit report from TransUnion, one of the UK’s leading credit reference agencies, as well as guidance when their credit score changes and personalised tips about how to improve their credit status TotallyMoney analysis of 7,000 of its own new sign-ups shows that almost half (45%) of new customers with a “low” (sub-556) TransUnion credit score improved their credit score within six months of signing up to TotallyMoney. The biggest gains were achieved by people with the very Customers that made a habit of checking their report every month achieved a 2.3x (133%) bigger score increase than less engaged customers, on average Nik Charalampous, TotallyMoney CEO (pictured), said: “This is a massive TotallyMoney milestone! Six million people in the UK have taken control of their financial future and gained the knowledge they need to understand and improve their credit status with our free app.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
